04 · Decision brief

Three findings that matter

These conclusions apply to all 103 records returned by the official Harvard Library space finder on 21 September 2026.

01

Capacity is concentrated.

Lamont and Widener account for 992 of 2,098 listed seats (47%), even though they contain only 27 of 103 space records. Large open rooms shape system capacity.

02

Noise and task pull apart.

Only 45 spaces are coded Silent or Whispers; 58 are coded Chatter. A single “best library” ranking would hide the difference between focused work and collaboration.

03

Equipment is not universal.

45 spaces are reservable, 32 list a display, and 27 list a whiteboard. Those gaps matter most for group and presentation work.

Recommended next moves

Make the information more decision-ready.

  1. Protect quiet capacity while improving wayfinding.Label Silent and Whispers zones consistently at the entrance and online; monitor whether the 45 lower-noise records match student expectations.
  2. Target collaboration upgrades.Prioritize rooms that are already reservable but lack a listed display or whiteboard, then verify the physical inventory before purchasing.
  3. Add anonymous demand evidence.Collect periodic occupied-seat counts by broad time block and a short feature-priority survey—without names, contact details, or device tracking.
